semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Both terms "pre-training techniques" and "pre-training" refer to the same concept of training a model or part of a model on a data set prior to the main task-specific training.

parent_domains.justification: Training is a broader category that encompasses pre-training as a type of preliminary training step.
Pre-training techniques are part of the strategies used in optimization and training of models, which is a broader category.
This encompasses all forms of training, including pre-training, as part of the larger framework of preparing a model.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Among the parent domains, "training" directly relates to pre-training as it forms the foundational process before the specific task-related fine-tuning, making it the closest parent.

child_domains.justification: It is a specific technique under the broader umbrella of pre-training techniques focusing on learning representations by contrasting positive and negative pairs.
This is a specialized application of pre-training techniques specifically for language models.
A specialized form of pre-training techniques focused on learning from image-text pairs.

closest_child_domain.justification: Given "pre-training techniques" as the domain, "language model pre-training" is a direct and highly focused application, frequently discussed within the same context.

sibling_domains.justification: Pre-finetuning is closely related as it often follows or complements pre-training in the training pipeline.
This is generally the result of applying pre-training techniques and shares foundational knowledge requirements and methods.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Pre-finetuning follows pre-training directly in the training pipeline, making it the most closely associated sibling domain.

unrelated_domains.justification: This domain is unrelated as it pertains to skills training outside of the technical and deep learning scope.
Motor learning is concerned with physiological processes, which do not directly relate to deep learning pre-training techniques.
While related to learning, learning theory is a broader concept not specific to the technical details of pre-training techniques.
